newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says Jan-Sept 1996 BOP at $3.7 bln.
newsitem.headline: Manila says Jan-Sept 1996 BOP at $3.7 bln.

text.p: The Philippines balance of payments (BOP) was at a surplus of $3.7 billion in the first nine months of 1996 compared with $783 million in the same period last year, the Central Bank said on Monday.
The bank has said previously that the BOP surplus, according to preliminary figures, was $4.2 billion at the end of the year.
"Behind this positive development was the strong performance of the capital and financial account which more than funded the higher current account deficit," the Central Bank said.

The current account deficit widened to $2.46 billion in the first nine months from $1.98 billion in the year-earlier period due to the higher merchandise trade deficit, the Central Bank said. It was equivalent to 3.9 percent of Gross National Product compared with 3.6 percent in the 1995 period.
The current account measures merchandise and non-merchandise trade, as well as transfers or donations.

Meanwhile, the surplus in the capital and financial account surged to $8.09 billion from $3.51 billion. This contained substantial inflows of medium and long-term loans as well as foreign investments which covered the current account deficit and resulted in a balance of payments surplus, the Central Bank said.
Net foreign investments, at $1.1 billion in the nine-month period, accounted for 13.9 percent of the capital and financial account surplus.

"What was notable in the investment pattern was that 53.9 percent of the total net inflows was accounted for by net foreign direct investments compared to the 47.4 percent share recorded last year," the Central Bank said.
This indicated the relative stability of inflows channelled to more permanent productive undertakings, it said.
